question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and what deterministic rules should decide allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout behavior for risky tool calls?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing gate, but the permanent behavior changes the core authorization boundary, config contract, transcript shape, and channel approval UX, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design The Core Gate
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout handling, and regression coverage around existing plugin approvals.

options.title: Keep Plugin-Only Approvals
options.body: Leave core behavior unchanged and require operators or plugins to enforce contextual approval through before_tool_call.requireApproval or trusted tool policies.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Policy Work
options.body: Wait for related action-level deny, response-gate, and HITL interrupt designs to converge before adding a new config surface.

recommendation.title: Design The Core Gate
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout handling, and regression coverage around existing plugin approvals.
